final_note: Control = causation. Lose control and you lose the inference.

concepts.def: IV occurs naturally; researcher measures its effect.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lab: high control, high internal validity, low ecological validity. Field: less control but more realistic. Natural: studies real events (e.g. ROmanian orphans). Quasi: IV is a participant variable, so no random allocation.

walkthroughs.h2: Repeated Measures vs Independent Groups vs Matched Pairs
walkthroughs.body_html: Repeated measures uses the same participants — reduces participant variables but risks order effects (use counterbalancing). Independent groups uses different participants — no order effects but more participant variability. Matched pairs compromises by matching participants on key variables.

Variables must be operationalised — anxiety becomes 'heart rate per minute'. Confounding variables vary with the IV and ruin inference. Extraneous variables are nuisance variables to control. Random allocation reduces both.
